newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal minister rejects IMF deficit advice.
newsitem.headline: Portugal minister rejects IMF deficit advice.

text.p: Finance Minister Antonio Sousa Franco said on Tuesday that an IMF remedy for dealing with Portugal's budget deficit -- wage freezes and job cuts -- was inappropriate and unnecessary.

The minister, who is in Washington for the International Monetary Fund's annual meeting, said that Portugal did not need to fire civil servants and public sector workers or raise Value Added Tax (VAT), another IMF recommendation.
"It is not necessary to fire public sector workers or raise IVA to achieve our budget objectives," he told local TSF radio in an interview.

The Socialist government is drawing up its plans for cutting the deficit to three percent of gross domestic product (GDP) in 1997 -- the threshhold for Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) -- from an estimated four percent this year. The IMF said this could only be done by taking tough action.
"They (the IMF recommendations) are completely inadequate for the Portuguese situation," Sousa Franco said.
"The report mentions classic remedies taken from (economic) manuals but we are going to act in accordance with Portuguese reality and not in accordance the manuals," he said.
